# Discover

*Product* · also written Google Discover

Google's personalised feed of articles and videos, shown without a query, with its own report in Search Console.

**Glossary** (*Google Discover*): Google's Discover surface: indexed content that meets Discover's content policies is eligible automatically, with no special tags or structured data, and Discover uses many of the same signals and systems as Search.

Narrative: the topic [Google Discover](../topics/discover.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

28 claims mention it: 8 from Google's documentation, 16 shown or said at the event (5 confirmed by Google docs, 8 consistent with Google docs, 3 nothing to verify), 4 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Discover content policies](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en).

- [`D1-C026`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Docs: Search profiles launched on 4 June 2026, in the US first, for creators and publishers with a sizable following on at least one major social or video platform. They appear in knowledge panels and Discover. `[D1-C026, docs, Google blog (4 June 2026), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/a-new-profile-to-help-publishers-and-creators-highlight-their-work-on-search/]`
- [`D1-C030`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Docs: The Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover. Excluding removes both links to the site and use of its content to ground answers. `[D1-C030, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en]`
- [`D1-C062`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Docs: Google's guide for generative AI features recommends the Generative AI performance report in Search Console for measuring how content performs in generative AI features on Google Search and Discover. `[D1-C062, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide]`
- [`D3-C219`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Docs: Google's Discover documentation says content is automatically eligible for Discover if it is indexed and meets Discover's content policies, needs no special tags or structured data, and is not guaranteed to appear. `[D3-C219, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover]`
- [`D3-C220`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Docs: Google's Discover documentation says Discover uses many of the same signals and systems as Search to determine what is helpful, people-first content. `[D3-C220, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover]`
- [`D3-C227`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Docs: Google's Discover documentation says to specify the large image with schema.org markup or the og:image meta tag, which can influence the thumbnail Discover chooses, and that a vertical image cropped to 16x9 must keep its important details. `[D3-C227, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover]`
- [`D3-C229`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Docs: Google's Discover content policies ask news sources for clear dates and bylines, information about the authors, publication and publisher, and contact information, and say repeated or egregious violations can make a site ineligible for Discover. `[D3-C229, docs, Google Search Help, https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C467`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Docs: Google's help page says platform properties show only how content performs on Google Search, Discover and Google News, not how often it is seen on the social or video platform itself. `[D3-C467, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/17148418?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C087`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The max-image-preview rule sets the maximum size of a page's image previews: none shows no preview, standard a default-sized one and large the largest possible, for example in Discover. `[D2-C087, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C222`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide defined E-E-A-T: experience means first-hand, personal experience with the topic, expertise the necessary knowledge or skill, and authoritativeness the extent to which the creator or website is known as a go-to source for the topic. `[D3-C222, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C223`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide said trust comes first: untrustworthy pages have low E-E-A-T however experienced, expert or authoritative they seem. `[D3-C223, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C224`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide recommended large images at least 1,200 px wide, with more than 300,000 total pixels and a 16x9 aspect ratio, enabled by the max-image-preview:large setting. `[D3-C224, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C225`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Discover slide said to avoid generic images, such as a site logo, and text-heavy images. `[D3-C225, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C089`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: max-image-preview:large matters mainly in Discover, where it allows a large image that draws people's attention, so the rule can make a page more visible than leaving it out, John Mueller said. `[D2-C089, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C525`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: An image Google has extracted can appear almost anywhere Google shows results, including Discover, image search, web search and AI features, so its potential reach is immense. `[D2-C525, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C549`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Videos can appear in the main search results, in video-specific result tabs and in Discover (the tab names are unclear in the recording). `[D2-C549, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C936`](../sessions/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Setting the max-image-preview robots meta tag to large can make content perform surprisingly well in Discover, Gary Illyes said. `[D2-C936, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C749`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google Discover is not included in Google Trends, because Discover is a content feed with no search box, while Trends counts only the queries people type into Google Search or YouTube. `[D2-C749, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C218`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's Discover slide showed an eligibility gate: content with a policy violation goes to a policy compliance check and low-quality content to an E-E-A-T quality check, and both can end with the content filtered out, while safe and trusted content becomes eligible for Discover. `[D3-C218, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C221`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's Discover slide said that for eligible content image quality decides click-through: a small thumbnail lowers the click-through rate and a large, high-resolution image raises it. `[D3-C221, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C226`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's Discover slide said images are subject to the same policy requirements as the content and that misleading, exaggerated or outrageous images should be avoided. `[D3-C226, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C148`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: The keynote's third driver was that information quality remains a core focus for Google, which wants high-quality sources to serve across Google Search, its AI experiences in Search, YouTube and Discover. `[D1-C148, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C092`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: John Mueller speculated that the use of max-video-preview may change in future, for example in Discover, where letting people view a full video could make sense. `[D2-C092, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C228`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Slide, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's closing Discover slide pointed to the Discover content policies in Google Search Help and to the Search Central documentation. `[D3-C228, slide, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C751`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Analysis: Google Trends cannot show demand that reaches people through the Discover feed, so Discover visibility has to be judged from Search Console's Discover performance report rather than from Trends. `[D2-C751, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C230`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Analysis: For Discover, set max-image-preview:large on article templates, give every article a relevant image at least 1,200 px wide in og:image or schema.org markup that is neither the site logo nor text-heavy, and show clear bylines and dates. `[D3-C230, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C435`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: Review the filters and regexes that Search Console's AI-powered configuration proposes before trusting the numbers: Google's launch post calls the feature experimental, warns that AI can misinterpret requests, and limits it to the Search results Performance report (not Discover or News) and to configuration, not sorting or exporting. `[D3-C435, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C441`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: Search Console's generative AI performance reports count impressions only, with no clicks and no query dimension (Google documents the Search report for AI Overviews and AI Mode, plus a separate Discover report), so measure visits that follow AI answers with your own analytics. `[D3-C441, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-04` **SHOULD** · Documented: Allow full snippets and large previews with max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-10` **MAY** · Documented: Use the Search generative AI setting in Search Console only to take a property out of AI Overviews and AI Mode (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IMG-07` **SHOULD** · Documented: Give every article a large, relevant lead image and declare it in og:image or markup (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-07` **MAY** · Documented: Track AI feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-09` **MAY** · Documented: Add the brand's YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X accounts to Search Console as platform properties (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
